name: UX & Behavioral Design
description: Public-domain principles for interface reviews, each with an axiom, a trigger, a checklist and a citation.

rules.title: UX & Behavioral Design Rules
rules.intro:
Apply these rules when reviewing or writing interface code. Each card names one
public-domain principle, when to check for it, and the concrete fix.

skill.name: ux-laws
skill.description: Review or write interface code against the UX & Behavioral Design deck — {cards} public-domain principles. Use when auditing layouts, forms, navigation, or touch targets. Start with the index below, then read the one resource file for the area you are checking.
skill.title: UX & Behavioral Design
skill.intro:
This file is the index. The cards themselves live in `resources/`, one
file per category. Use the tables below to decide which file to open, then
read that file. Do not load every resource unless the change spans several
categories.
commonRules: Prefer the smallest change that removes the failure state.
Check the code in front of you; do not restyle unrelated code.

A checklist item that asks for a human-subject experiment cannot be
  satisfied by reading code. Say so rather than claiming it was done.
skill.footer: Every card cites one primary paper; the citation travels with the card.
